requirement:
Rendering the view of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST NOT invoke an
assessment model. It MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.render_only`.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.render_only` has two obligations:
1. Rendering the file-notes view MUST NOT invoke an assessment model.
2. The render MUST follow `requirements.test-coverage.index.render_only`. That cited requirement covers reading no saved execution measurements, not evaluating exception acceptance, and not auditing review freshness. It is context only; I did not reassess its own tests.

**How a test can observe the no-model obligation.** The notes renderer, `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#fn[pages]`, takes only a root path, a file set and an index path. It has no completion-provider parameter. The model-invoking code (`src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[assess]` and `fn[assess_subject]`) takes a `CompletionProvider`. So a model call from the render path would show up as one of these:
- a review file written or rewritten;
- a missing, invalid or stale review shown as something other than its stored state;
- a created `target` artifact.

The tests check each of these.

**Test mapping.**
- `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[each_render_reads_current_notes_and_keeps_recorded_reviews_without_writing]`:
  - It renders the notes page for a file with a saved review.
  - It then changes the source so the review no longer matches the source.
  - It re-renders and asserts that the page shows the current explanation and still shows `Recorded review: **Recorded true**`.
  - It asserts that the page does not say "citations changed".
  - It asserts that the saved review bytes are unchanged and that no `target` directory was created.
  - A model re-assessment of the stale review would change the review file or its display, so the test would catch it.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[overview_shows_missing_unreadable_and_recorded_reviews_with_current_justifications]`:
  - It covers the review states missing, recorded true, recorded false, recorded FIXME, invalid JSON, and unreadable (a directory in place of the file).
  - For each state it asserts that the label is the stored state, for example "Missing", "Unreadable" or "Recorded true".
  - A missing review must stay "Missing" on render, so nothing was assessed.
  - It asserts that "current and accepted" and "input is stale" are absent, so no freshness or acceptance audit ran.
  - It changes the source against a saved review and asserts that the review bytes are unchanged and that the review still reads "Recorded true".
  - It asserts that no `target` directory exists.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts]`:
  - It populates the book with and without a saved coverage attempt, including invalid or empty `attempt.json`.
  - It asserts that the rendered chapters are identical in every case, so saved measurements do not affect the output.
  - It asserts that the saved attempt files are untouched and that no selection cache is created.
  - It asserts that the file-notes chapter is generated as `File notes: code.rs`.
  - This covers the `index.render_only` side: no saved measurements are read and nothing is written.

**Gaps.** I found none. No test injects a mock model provider. That is not required here, because the render path has no provider to inject and the tests assert the observable absence of any assessment effect across missing, unreadable, stale and recorded review inputs. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
